name: wheel-picker

frames.best_why: The drums are settled on 9:41 AM with the selection band clear and no cursor over the numbers.

tagline: Three tiny drums of numbers spin under a highlight bar to set a time.
summary: An iOS-style time picker with three vertical drums for hour, minute and AM/PM. Rows curve away in perspective above and below a grey selection band; drag or flick a drum and it coasts then snaps to a value.
appearance: A rounded dark card holds three narrow columns of numbers under a pill-shaped grey band that marks the chosen hour, minute and AM/PM. Numbers shrink and fade toward the top and bottom edges.
behaviour: Each column turns like a drum as you drag it, with the rows above and below curving away. A flick keeps it coasting before it settles on a row, and keyboard arrows step it by one.
demo_content: Wake me up at, set to 9:41 am then 2:39 am.
search_phrases: spin the drum to set time
use_when: A settings form needs to set a time quickly on touch, with the familiar iOS drum feel.
avoid_when: It is tall, needs room for three columns, and precise values are slower than typing into a field.
customise: Columns with options and labels, controlled or default value, a change callback and the group label are props; row styling is in the source.
weight_why: Three columns with one transform each; springs run only while spinning.

a11y.note: Each drum is a labelled spinbutton with keyboard steps and a visible focus ring; the 3D band is a visual cue only.

polish_why: Very close to the native picker with clean 3D rows; outer numbers nearly vanish on black.
